newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FUND VIEW - Jardine says bullish on Malaysia stocks.
newsitem.headline: FUND VIEW - Jardine says bullish on Malaysia stocks.

text.p: International fund manager Jardine Fleming on Tuesday said it was time for medium and long-term investors to start buying again on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE).
The fund manager said stock prices, which have fallen nearly 26 percent this year, most of it since March, were trading at very attractive levels.
"From a fundamental perspective now is a good time to be a cash buyer of this market," said Simon Crinage, chief executive of Jardine Fleming Apex Unit Trusts Bhd.
Jardine Fleming Apex is a joint venture between Jardine Fleming and Apex Equity Holdings Bhd, a company listed on the KLSE.

"You have a market that is trading at a prospective earnings of 13.7 times. In 1986, when Malaysia had a negative GDP growth of one percent, this market was trading on 15 times (price-to-earnings ratio)," he said.
"Now you have an economy that is growing at 8.0 to 8.2 percent a year and you have a market trading on 13.7 times," he said at the launch of JF Apex Malaysia Growth Trust fund.
Malaysian stocks have suffered after a series of policy moves perceived as ill-timed, a sharp fall of the Malaysian ringgit and fears about the economy's direction.

Jardine Fleming Apex Unit Trusts officials said the fund, the new company's first, was expected to do well despite the bearish stock market. Its initial size was expected to be 100 million ringgit ($36 million), they said.

Crinage said it has approval to raise up to 500 million ringgit at five ringgit per unit. The fund will have a net asset value of 4.75 ringgit each during the initial offer period, which ends on August 26.
"A lot (of the performance of the fund) depends on how investors perceive this product. We have to undergo a lengthy educational process in this market," he said.
He said the fund introduces several firsts to the Malaysian market. It will not pay any dividend and pricing for purposes of repurchase will be based on net asset value (NAV).
"The fund's NAV will be calculated on a daily basis," Crinage said.

He said the new fund would draw upon the success of its existing Hong Kong-based JF Malaysia Trust, which has gained over 223 percent, or 26.5 percent per annum, over the last five years, against the KLSE Composite Index's 76 percent gain.
Though outperforming the Composite Index, the JF Malaysia Trust's NAV has dropped some 20 percent this year.
He said it was a U.S. dollar-denominated fund and about six to seven percent of the loss was due to currency factors.
"On the equity performance of the portfolio, it is down something in the region of 13 percent against the Composite Index, which I believe is down some 24 percent," he said in reply to questions.
Jardine Fleming said there were redemptions in the JF Malaysia Trust this year due to the market turmoil.

"(Redemption) has been relatively light and I think international investor sentiment is that the fundamentals of the Malaysian market are good," said Tim Freshwater, group deputy chairman of Jardine Fleming Ltd.
